I am an old woman, 69 years, and I farm this small piece of land near my house with cassava and cocoyam together. I have no money for chemical fertilizer this season, and even if government brings it, the price is too much for me — I will use the small household refuse and ash from my kitchen instead. I plant the cassava stems I kept from last harvest, like my mother taught me, and I do the work myself with help from my grandchildren when school closes. The rain here in the South East comes well, so I do not need to fetch water for the farm.
